newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavaria defends deportation of Bosnian refugees.
newsitem.headline: Bavaria defends deportation of Bosnian refugees.

text.p: The German state of Bavaria, responding to U.S. criticism, said on Thursday that while it had deported about 100 Bosnian refugees and encourged the return of many more, it was not forcing them to go to home areas they fled during wartime ethnic cleansing.

Where the reugees go after they get to Bosnia is the responsibility of the Bosnian government in Sarajevo, State interior minister Guenter Beckstein said in a statement, citing a German-Bosnian agreement signed last December.
U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Wednesday that it was "premature to return forcibly Bosnians to areas where their ethnic group is in the minority".
He cited recent repression by Croatians against minority Serbs in the Krajina region and violence in eastern Slavonia as evidence that conditions were not yet ripe for a return of all refugees.

There are still some 300,000 Bosnian refugees in Germany, most of them Moslems driven out of areas now ruled by Serbs, and cash-strapped German officials are increasingly determined that they should go back to Bosnia soon.

Burns urged Germany to work closely with the United Nations on repatriation of refugees "to differentiate, to distinguish, between Bosnians from areas where their ethnic group is in the minority and those from areas where their ethnic group is in the majority."
Conservative Bavaria has been among the German states most active in sending back Bosnian refugees.

Beckstein said in his statement: "(Deportations) are not made to defined regions of origin, but to Sarajevo, where Bosnian authories who have been informed in advance (of their arrival) take over their further distribution."
A ministry spokesman, who asked not to be named, said Bavaria resorted to occasional forcible repatriation only after refugees denied further residence refused to leave.
Since starting this programme, he said, about 10,000 of the 65,000 Bosnians in Bavaria had left voluntarily, roughly half of the total that had already left from all of Germany.
